 Position Overview
   

  

 As a Robotics Software Engineer, you will work closely with senior engineers to bring hardware prototypes to life and build essential software tools that support our robotic platforms. In this hands\-on role, you will assist in integrating new hardware components, developing diagnostic and control interfaces, and maintaining ROS 2 nodes. If you enjoy working with physical systems, writing practical C\+\+ and Python code, and building usable tools across hardware\-software boundaries, this role offers an exciting opportunity to grow your technical skills on real\-world systems.
   

  

**Responsibilities**
* Integrate new hardware prototypes with the robot’s software systems.
* Rapidly develop proof\-of\-concept software for evaluating new components and designs.
* Build control, configuration, visualization, and diagnostic GUIs for engineers and operators.
* Create reusable tools for hardware bring\-up, testing, calibration, data collection, and troubleshooting.
* Develop and maintain ROS 2 nodes, interfaces, drivers, and supporting applications.
* Work with hardware engineers to define software interfaces and translate prototype requirements into working systems.
* Test integrated hardware/software behavior, analyze logs and telemetry, and diagnose issues across subsystem boundaries.
* Improve successful prototypes into reliable, documented, and maintainable engineering tools.
* Contribute to automated testing, simulation, deployment infrastructure, and other robotics software projects as priorities require.
* Participate in design discussions, code reviews, documentation, and field or lab testing.


**Requirements**
* 0–2 years of experience in robotics software, embedded systems, or hands\-on engineering projects.
* Practical C\+\+ and Python ability.
* Software fundamentals and debugging skills.
* Comfort working with physical systems and imperfect prototypes.
* Some ROS or robotics project experience, without requiring deep ROS 2/DDS expertise.
* Familiarity with common communication interfaces or protocols—such as CAN, serial, Ethernet, or USB—if those match the hardware.
* Ability to build simple user\-facing tools or GUIs.
* A bias toward experimentation, iteration, and completing usable prototypes.
* Clear communication with engineers from different disciplines.


 Nice to Have
   

  

* Hands\-on experience with hardware bring\-up, microcontroller development, or sensor integration.
* Familiarity with simulation environments (Gazebo, Isaac Sim, MuJoCo) or containerization (Docker).
* Educational background or degree in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field.
* Open\-source contributions or personal robotics projects.
